title: Serial UART & Wireless Communication
summary: Connect Arduinos to computers, Bluetooth modules, and GPS with asynchronous TX/RX serial streams.

steps.title: Asynchronous Streams & Baud Framing
steps.markdownContent: To roam untethered across terrain, robots transmit commands wirelessly using **UART** (Universal Asynchronous Receiver-Transmitter). Unlike I2C or SPI, UART is **asynchronous**—there is no shared clock line! Both devices agree on a precise bit frequency (the **Baud Rate**, such as 9600 bits per second) and synchronize on the falling edge of a Start Bit.

steps.title: Crossed Wires: TX to RX
steps.markdownContent:
The golden wiring rule of UART serial is to **cross the lines**:

- Arduino `TX` (Transmit) connects to Module `RX` (Receive).
- Module `TX` connects to Arduino `RX`.
- Pins `0` and `1` are hardwired to the onboard USB chip. To avoid USB upload collisions, we use the `<SoftwareSerial.h>` library to create virtual serial ports on pins `10` and `11`!

steps.title: Voltage Divider Protection for 3.3V RX
steps.markdownContent:
Examine the HC-05 Bluetooth Module (`comp_29`):
1. Module `TXD` outputs safe 3.3V logic—connect directly to Uno Pin `10` (`SoftwareSerial RX`).
2. Module `RXD` cannot tolerate 5.0V! Build a resistor divider on breadboard:
   - Connect Uno Pin `11` (`TX`) to a 1kΩ resistor.
   - Connect the resistor to a node wired to Module `RXD`.
   - Connect a 2kΩ resistor from the node to `GND`.
   - Voltage drops safely: $5\text{V} \times \frac{2\text{k}\Omega}{1\text{k}\Omega + 2\text{k}\Omega} = 3.33\text{V}$!

questions.question: What is the golden wiring rule for connecting two UART serial devices?
options: Cross the data lines: TX connects to RX, and RX connects to TX
Connect TX to TX, and RX to RX

questions.question: Why is UART called 'asynchronous'?
options: There is no shared clock line; timing is governed entirely by agreed baud rates
It only works when the microcontroller is asleep
Signals are sent in reverse order

questions.question: Why should you avoid connecting external hardware to Digital Pins 0 and 1 on an Uno?
options: Pins 0 and 1 are shared with the onboard USB-to-serial chip used for flashing code

questions.question: What is the purpose of the SoftwareSerial library?
options: It allows ordinary digital pins to emulate hardware UART serial ports
It compresses sketches to save flash memory

questions.question: Why is a voltage divider needed between an Uno TX pin and a 3.3V Bluetooth module RX pin?
options: To step down the 5V Arduino signal to prevent overvoltage damage to the 3.3V module

questions.question: What method checks how many bytes are waiting in the serial receive buffer?
What happens if the transmitter and receiver are configured with mismatched baud rates?
options: Bits are sampled at incorrect intervals, resulting in corrupt or unreadable data
